name: two_parallel_faces_and_it_says_so
why: The measuring tool on two faces: distance, and whether they are parallel or perpendicular. The two large faces of a plate are parallel and 10 apart; they are not perpendicular, and that «no» is an expectation too -- a field that always answered «true» would pass half the cases.
_already_seen_red: `IMeasure.Calculate(Object Entities)` TAKES AN ARGUMENT AND DOES NOT LOOK AT IT: it measures what is SELECTED. Measured on 15/9/2026: called with a vector of two faces it answers FALSE; with the same two faces selected and the argument null it answers TRUE and gives 0.01. And called with ONE face in the array, while the selection still contained two, it answered TRUE and gave the area of both -- 3200 mm2 instead of 1600. A believable number, from the right part, of another selection. The operation now empties the selection, selects by hand and looks at the boolean.

expect.tolerance_why: the thickness of the plate, given in metres

expect.why: the «no» is an expectation too: a field that always answers true would pass half the cases

expect.tolerance_why: two faces of 40x40: the total area is the sum, and that is how you see whether it measured BOTH the things it was given
